answer: Rotating Assignment Lottery. Each round, a public verifiable random function derives from the latest block a seed unknown before that block. Agents are assigned tasks by mapping that seed against their registered identity hash. A duplicate identity is a hollow copy that only wins tasks when the seed happens to match, so cloning yields no shared advantage. An attacker running many clones faces an echo of split rewards: each duplicate must independently fund compute and monitoring, paying full per-identity cost with no guaranteed return.
